stories.label: A Scaramucci or a Zacharia? A new unit of time for the Trump White House
stories.summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia was pushed out after five days, hours after Trump publicly told her to 'reconsider her role' after a rocky debut, the shortest tenure on record for the post. Lead with the five days and how she went; the structural point is a White House turning over the people who speak for it while it fights an unpopular war in Iran three weeks before the midterms. Keep it factual, not gossip. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Ukraine's Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Trump
stories.summary: New development past the shadow-fleet story: Ukraine's 'Operation Vivaldi' has retaken more occupied ground in Donetsk while Washington lifts oil sanctions on Russia and buys its diesel, and Zelenskyy took his case to EU leaders in Brussels. Lead with the gap: Kyiv is gaining on the battlefield just as its main backer eases pressure on Moscow, leaving Europe to decide whether to fill it. Prediction markets now put Russia-Ukraine peace talks by 30 November at 19%, down from 50% a week ago. Datelined Kyiv or Brussels.

stories.label: Saudi-led coalition says it downed drones and missiles over Riyadh, Red Sea, Yanbu
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it shot down drones over Riyadh and cruise missiles over the Red Sea and near Yanbu, the Red Sea terminal Saudi Arabia uses to export crude without passing through Hormuz. Lead with Yanbu: with Hormuz closed, the bypass route is now under fire, and that is what holds Brent crude near its highest since mid-September (above $109 on Friday). Name Brent crude and ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb. Attribute the interception claims to coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki. Datelined Riyadh.

stories.label: How Israeli firm's 'zero-click' malware attack poses global security risk
stories.summary: Researchers (Citizen Lab) traced the first known spyware delivered through online advertising to Israeli firm Candiru: loading a page or refreshing an app that shows an ad is enough to compromise a phone or laptop, with no click. Lead with the delivery mechanism: the ad-tech supply chain every site and app uses has become an infection channel, so targeting no longer needs a lure. Name who was targeted where the sources say, and the export-licensing regime that lets the firm sell.

stories.label: En EE. UU. Alexander Ardón confesó 56 asesinatos, narcotráfico y sobornos; en Honduras lo juzgaron por seis millones de lempiras y salió libre
stories.summary: Former El Paraíso mayor Alexander Ardón confessed to 56 murders, drug trafficking and bribing officials before a US court, yet the only case Honduras ever brought him to trial on was laundering six million lempiras, and he was acquitted. Lead with the 56 against the one acquittal; the mechanism is a justice system that left narco-politicians to US prosecutors, so the victims at home never got a case. Datelined Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: Locais de votação alterados e abstenção: estigma afasta eleitores da Maré das urnas
stories.summary: Ahead of Brazil's presidential runoff, Rio's electoral court (TRE-RJ) moved polling stations out of the Maré favela complex on security grounds, without explaining the decision, and a local organisation links it to high abstention there. Lead with who loses the vote: residents of one of Rio's largest favelas made to travel out of their neighbourhood to cast a ballot. The mechanism is 'security' used to redraw access to the vote for poor, Black voters. Datelined Rio de Janeiro.

stories.label: Maina's son, Faisal, arrested after six years on the run - Report
stories.summary: Faisal Maina, son of convicted pension-fund chief Abdulrasheed Maina, has reportedly been arrested after six years as a fugitive; he jumped bail in 2020 on EFCC money-laundering charges tied to his father's pension scandal. Lead with the six years and the bail he skipped; the accountability point is that the pensions stolen by the old Pension Reform Task Team belonged to retired civil servants, and the case shows how long Nigeria takes to bring the families of the convicted to court. Say it is reported, not yet confirmed by the EFCC, if the source says so. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: EU plans new tool to restrict market access in potential trade war
stories.summary: Von der Leyen told EU leaders the Commission will build a tool to swiftly restrict access to the single market in a trade war, as France and Germany push for stronger powers against China. Lead with what it changes: the bloc's biggest asset, access to 450 million consumers, would become a fast weapon rather than a years-long procedure. TRT World is Turkish state media; attribute accordingly. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: While Software Ate the World, This Company Ate Its Own Software Business
stories.summary: Chinese AI firm DataCanvas made 76.5% of its revenue from AI foundation software in 2023; by the first half of 2026, as it files for a Hong Kong IPO, that business had almost vanished from its sales. Lead with the collapse of the share and what replaced it; the mechanism is China's AI market paying for compute and hardware, not software, which reshapes which AI firms can list.

stories.label: 京东双十一取消定金预售，押注服务消费推上百项产品
stories.summary: JD.com has scrapped deposit-based pre-sales for this year's Singles' Day, the 18th, and is pushing more than a hundred service products instead. Lead with the end of the pre-sale, the mechanism that defined China's biggest shopping festival; the structural point is slowing e-commerce growth forcing platforms to compete on delivery and services rather than price, a read on Chinese household spending. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses found recording audio without wearers' consent
stories.summary: Some Ray-Ban Meta glasses recorded conversations without the 'Hey Meta' wake phrase, so neither the wearer nor the people around them knew; Meta says a bug caused it and has been fixed. Lead with the people recorded who never agreed to anything; the mechanism is an always-listening microphone on a face, where a software fault turns into covert surveillance of bystanders. Say what Meta has not disclosed: how long, how many devices, and where the audio went.

stories.label: 兑现度的胜利，星尘智能再融10亿
stories.summary: Chinese robotics firm Stardust Intelligence (Astribot) has raised another 1 billion yuan, while investors in China's humanoid and embodied-AI boom grow pickier about who delivers. Lead with the round and what investors now demand (delivered units and revenue, not demos); the structural point is China's state-backed push into robots moving from hype to a shakeout.

stories.label: F-22 Pilot Controls FQ-44 Fighter Drone From The Cockpit For The First Time
stories.summary: For the first time, an F-22 pilot directed an FQ-44 Collaborative Combat Aircraft drone from the cockpit in flight. Lead with the milestone: one human now commands an armed autonomous wingman in the air, the model the US Air Force plans to field at scale. The question to raise is how much targeting the drone decides for itself and who is accountable when it does.

stories.label: What is the 'Mother of All Bombs' US could use in Iran?
stories.summary: New development in the Gulf war arc: Trump on Thursday declined to rule out dropping the GBU-43 MOAB on Iran. Lead with the mismatch: an 11-tonne air-burst bomb built for caves and troops in the open cannot reach enrichment halls buried under a mountain at Fordow, so the threat lands on people and surface sites, not the nuclear programme. Datelined Tehran; carry the Al Jazeera and Dawn framing alongside Bloomberg's.

stories.label: Pope Leo XIV requests a truce from Putin to deliver aid to Oleshky
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV phoned Putin and asked for a local truce so aid can reach Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town on the Dnipro's left bank cut off from supplies and evacuation. Lead with the civilians trapped there; set the Vatican and Meduza accounts against TASS's version, in which Putin blamed Kyiv for the humanitarian situation while endorsing the Vatican's effort. Datelined Oleshky.

stories.label: Chile's president makes first state visit to Bolivia in 71 years as region shifts right
stories.summary: José Antonio Kast is the first Chilean leader on a state visit to Bolivia in 71 years; the two countries have had no full diplomatic relations since 1978 over Bolivia's lost coastline. Lead with the 71 years; the mechanism is a shared rightward turn (Kast and Rodrigo Paz) and alignment with Washington overriding a century-old sea-access grievance. Datelined La Paz.

stories.label: El Niño has killed hundreds of children in Sudan | New Scientist
stories.summary: Drought from the record El Niño has already killed hundreds of children in Sudan through starvation and disease, and famine risk is growing. Lead with the child deaths; the mechanism is a climate shock landing on a population the RSF-army war has already displaced and cut off from aid, so the drought kills through the war. Filed as politics, not science: it is a humanitarian disaster. Datelined in Darfur if the source names a place.

stories.label: As Sisi vows to leave power by 2030, sources differ on whether he really means it
stories.summary: Sisi told an armed forces symposium that Egypt's constitution 'would not be touched', which implies he leaves office when his term ends in 2030, in the same speech that warned against a return to the protests of 2011. Lead with the pledge and the warning side by side; Mada Masr's sources inside the state disagree on whether it is meant, and the 2019 amendments that extended his rule are the precedent. Datelined Cairo.

stories.label: В Кыргызстане признали экстремистской деятельность оппозиционного движения «Шумкар» — туда входят Кенжебаев и Болтурук
stories.summary: Kyrgyzstan has declared the opposition movement Shumkar 'extremist': a political blogger who was detained in Vietnam and brought home (Syrgak Kenzhebaev), an ecologist, a political analyst and the former external manager of the Kumtor gold mine (Tengiz Bolturuk). Lead with the rendition from Vietnam; the mechanism is the extremism label, which makes membership or support a crime and shuts opposition down under Japarov. Datelined Bishkek.

stories.label: From 95,000 to 60,000 Pilgrims: How Nigeria lost Hajj seats, as citizens raise concerns
stories.summary: Within two Hajj seasons Nigeria's pilgrim allocation fell from 95,000 to 60,000, so tens of thousands who saved for years must postpone a religious obligation. Lead with the 35,000 lost seats; explain the mechanism (how the Saudi quota and Nigeria's own allocation and welfare failures cut the number) and who decides. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: HSBC’s Islamic fund ploughs $38m in Palantir Technologies
stories.summary: An HSBC sharia-compliant fund put $38m into Palantir, whose software supplies the Israeli military and US immigration enforcement. Lead with the gap between Islamic finance's screens (interest, alcohol, gambling) and what they ignore (weapons and surveillance work); Muslim savers are the ones whose money sits in this. Datelined Dubai.

stories.label: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
stories.summary: Meta's new commercial terms will require business accounts to let Meta train AI on their linked website content, not just their posts. Lead with the reach: any publisher or shop with a Facebook page grants a licence that Meta would otherwise pay millions for, and opting out means leaving the platform. The economic mechanism is terms of service replacing licensing deals.

stories.label: Here’s What Telegram Giving Data to the U.S. Government Looks Like
stories.summary: Newly filed court records include a letter in which Telegram handed user data to US authorities under a court order. Lead with the document itself: the first concrete look at what a platform marketed as beyond government reach actually hands over, since the policy change after Durov's arrest in France. Users relying on Telegram for safety (activists, journalists, dissidents) are the ones affected.

stories.label: Meta bloqueia conteúdos políticos pró-Lula e contra Flávio acusando terrorismo e nudez
stories.summary: New development in the Brazil runoff arc: Brazil's federal prosecutors (Ministério Público Federal) opened an investigation into Meta and X for violating free expression, after Meta blocked pro-Lula and anti-Flávio Bolsonaro posts by flagging them as terrorism and nudity. Lead with the probe; the mechanism is automated moderation misfiring on one side's campaign content days before the vote. Datelined São Paulo or Brasília as the source gives it.

stories.label: Quantum Alliance forms to defend 6.4 million vulnerable bitcoin against future threats
stories.summary: A new Quantum Alliance is organising to protect 6.4 million bitcoin, including Satoshi Nakamoto's 1.1 million, held in addresses whose public keys are exposed and could be cracked by a future quantum computer. Lead with the 6.4 million coins; the dilemma is that freezing or moving them breaks bitcoin's property-rights promise while doing nothing lets an attacker take them. Name bitcoin.

stories.label: Japan is launching a mission to Mars's largest moon Phobos | New Scientist
stories.summary: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft launches on 20 October to land on Phobos and bring samples back to Earth. Lead with the century-old question it should settle: whether Phobos is a captured asteroid or debris blasted off Mars by an impact, which the sample chemistry can tell apart. Japan, not the US or China, would be first to return material from the Mars system. Datelined Tanegashima.

stories.label: A distant supercluster of galaxies points to self-interacting dark matter
stories.summary: El Gordo, a colliding galaxy cluster seven billion light-years away with more than two quadrillion solar masses, is too big for its era under standard cold dark matter; new modelling finds it fits if dark matter particles interact with each other. Lead with the size problem; the mechanism is that self-interaction changes how cluster cores collide and separate, making a rare object plausible. Name the study and its limits.

stories.label: Fury as Trump envoy stays silent after Americans are 'severely' beaten abroad: report
stories.summary: Israeli settlers beat Palestinian olive pickers and a Washington Post photojournalist and set groves alight in the occupied West Bank on Friday, one of several attacks on the harvest. Lead with the victims by name and number where the sources give them; the mechanism is the olive harvest as the economic lifeline settlers target every October, under army protection. The new detail is that Americans were among those beaten and US ambassador Mike Huckabee said nothing — name that silence as the accountability gap.

stories.label: If rights not observed, restrictions to continue in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's army commander-in-chief Amir Hatami says the Strait of Hormuz is under the 'full supervision' of the army and the IRGC and will stay closed until 'the enemy respects the rights of the Iranian people' — a stated condition for reopening, after two ships sank and a tanker burned this week. Lead with the condition and who sets it; tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Iran's army spokesman separately told Mehr that new operational plans will push US vessels further away. Attribute Mehr's quotes as Iranian state media.

stories.label: Mauritius Extends Curfew for 3 Days After Widespread Unrest
stories.summary: Mauritius extended its night curfew for three more nights after the worst unrest since 1999. Lead with that benchmark and explain what set the island off and who is on the streets; the structural why is a small, tourism- and offshore-finance-dependent economy where the 1999 riots after Kaya's death in custody still frame race and policing. Use only the Bloomberg link: the other two URLs in this cluster are CoreWeave stock stories mis-grouped by the feed.

stories.label: US in 'denuclearisation' talks with Russia and China: Trump
stories.summary: Trump says the US is in nuclear disarmament talks with Russia and China, and that China is racing to catch up on warheads. The mechanism: New START has lapsed, so no treaty now caps US or Russian deployed warheads, and China has never joined an arms-control framework. Lead with what is actually on the table and whether Moscow or Beijing confirm any talks; give the warhead counts for all three. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Short-term inflation surges to 11.38pc due to costly food
stories.summary: Pakistan's weekly price index (SPI) rose to 11.38% year on year in the week to October 15, with 23 of 51 essential items dearer. Lead with the specific staples and fuels that rose most and who pays: the lowest income quintile spends most of its budget on food. The structural why is the Hormuz energy shock passing through diesel and petrol into food transport; continue from the early-October report that inflation crossed 10%.

stories.label: IRH and Zambia's state miner resolve copper financing dispute
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's International Resources Holding — part of Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed's empire — and Zambia's state miner ZCCM-IH say they have settled their Mopani Copper Mines financing dispute, but the statement skirts the charges in ZCCM-IH's September letter. Lead with what ZCCM-IH alleged and what the settlement leaves unanswered; the mechanism is a Gulf sovereign-linked buyer taking control of an African copper asset Zambia had nationalised, and who holds the leverage now. Name copper as the series.

stories.label: Why is China buying up gold?
stories.summary: The People's Bank of China keeps adding gold to its reserves while Chinese households pile into the metal. Lead with the latest PBOC purchase figure and the run of consecutive months; the mechanism is de-dollarisation as sanctions insurance — reserves held in US Treasuries can be frozen, gold in Beijing cannot — plus households fleeing a weak property market. Name gold as the series and say what this does to the price.

stories.label: Scientists have just voted to abolish leap seconds | New Scientist
stories.summary: Representatives of 69 countries voted on 15 October to abolish the leap second: UTC will be allowed to drift up to an hour from Earth's rotation before any correction. Lead with the hour of drift; the mechanism is that leap seconds crash networks, GPS-linked systems and financial timestamps, while Earth's rotation has recently been speeding up, raising the prospect of a first-ever negative leap second. Say who opposed and why (Russia's GLONASS has been the holdout).

stories.label: 10 Malta-Italy flights disrupted by air traffic control failures
stories.summary: A data-network failure at Italy's air navigation provider ENAV cut air traffic management capacity across the country by 50%, cancelling and delaying flights at Rome Fiumicino, Milan Malpensa and beyond. Lead with the halved capacity and the single point of failure: one data transmission link between control centres grounded a national airspace. Say what failed, whether a cyberattack is ruled out, and how many flights were hit.

stories.label: 后摩智能亮出2D CIM+3D CIM路线！Agent竞速赛打响，双路径抢占端边算力先机
stories.summary: Chinese chip startup Houmo AI says its first 3D compute-in-memory chip, the A20, is in production, and its SRAM compute-in-memory M50 won 150 design-ins within a year — including a 300-gram Lenovo box that runs a 122-billion-parameter model offline at 50 tokens a second. Lead with that box; the mechanism is that inference is memory-bandwidth-bound, so computing inside SRAM sidesteps the HBM China cannot import under US export controls. A mainland view of how China is routing around the chip ban at the edge.

stories.label: How an extremist network articulated a hoax linking Brazil’s President Lula to child abuse on X
stories.summary: A distorted clip of Lula speaking about prostate exams was turned into a child-abuse hoax and went viral on X within hours, days before Brazil's tight runoff. Lead with the speed and the accounts that seeded it; the mechanism is a coordinated network and X's amplification, with no moderation brake, against an electoral court that has fought X before. Follows the Meta throttling of a Brazilian campaign and the polls showing Flávio Bolsonaro ahead.

stories.label: Moscow police detain suspected DataSuckers hackers linked to breaches in Ukraine and Russia
stories.summary: Russian police detained three suspected members of DataSuckers, a group tied to breaches in both Ukraine and Russia, after a hack of a popular restaurant chain exposed vast amounts of customer data. Lead with the rarity: Moscow seldom arrests hackers, and does so when Russians are the victims. Say how many customers' records leaked and what the group took from Ukrainian targets.

stories.label: CJP, Abhijeet Dipke: India's 'cockroach' protesters set to return despite police crackdown
stories.summary: India's Gen-Z 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement, born of anger at leaked national exam papers that decide entry to university and jobs, plans a flag march in Delhi after police warned its leader Abhijeet Dipke that Connaught Place 'is not a protest site' and a BJP minister accused it of disrupting Durga Puja. Lead with the state's response to a youth movement over exams; the structural why is a huge young cohort competing for scarce jobs, which the IMF named this week as the group most exposed to AI job loss.

stories.label: Syria's 2013 Baniyas massacres: What happened and who was Ali Kayali?
stories.summary: Ali Kayali, known as Mihrac Ural, the pro-Assad militia commander accused over the May 2013 massacres of Sunni civilians in al-Bayda and Ras al-Nabaa near Baniyas and wanted by Turkey for the 2013 Reyhanlı bombings that killed 52, was arrested on Thursday. Lead with the arrest and who made it; the accountability point is that a man tied to two of the war's worst mass killings went free for 13 years, and what court will now try him. TRT World is Turkish state media: attribute its account accordingly.

stories.label: Bend, Ore., is known for its outdoor charm.
stories.summary: A 16-year-old shot his way through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, with a long gun and killed three children aged 5, 8 and 11 and a teacher before a bystander shot him dead. Lead with the victims and the detail that locked doors, the main defence US schools have built, did not stop him; the mechanism is how a minor got a long gun. Dateline Bend.

stories.label: Warsh Vows Price Stability as A.I. Delivers 'Shock' to Economy
stories.summary: Fed chair Kevin Warsh, speaking at the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, called AI a 'shock' that complicates the inflation outlook and pledged price stability after hotter-than-expected US inflation, and markets now price a Fed hold in October. Lead with the Fed rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield: a central bank treating AI investment as an inflation shock rather than a productivity gift, and who pays for higher-for-longer rates (Global South borrowers forced to keep their own rates high).

stories.label: MSCI makes it official, and bitcoin (BTC) treasury firms Strategy, Metaplanet are on notice
stories.summary: MSCI has finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin, Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet among them, from its equity indexes. JPMorgan estimates $2.8 billion of forced selling of Strategy shares alone. Lead with the decision and the mechanism: index funds must sell the shares, not the bitcoin, so the hit lands on the treasury firms' ability to raise cheap equity to buy more. Name bitcoin as the series.

stories.label: World Bank sets fivefold minerals goal as Fed chairman Warsh flags financial stability risks | The National
stories.summary: The World Bank will grow its critical-minerals business fivefold over five years. Lead with the target and who it serves: mineral-rich developing countries, much of Africa among them, whose lithium, cobalt and copper are contested between Chinese refiners and Western buyers. The question is whether the Bank funds local processing or only extraction for export. Copper is the charted series. Keep Warsh to one line: he has his own story this cycle.

stories.label: Winter sea ice loss may be underestimated, ancient clues from a warmer Arctic suggest
stories.summary: Researchers checked climate models against the warm period 6,000 years ago and found future Arctic winter sea ice will likely shrink by about 1 million square km more than models project, an area roughly the size of Egypt. Lead with the number. The mechanism is the past used as a test the models failed: the models projecting the future under-predict loss.

stories.label: This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
stories.summary: The Prima retinal implant, a 2mm wireless photovoltaic chip under the retina fed by infrared light from camera glasses, is the first treatment to restore reading vision in advanced dry age-related macular degeneration, a disease of more than 5 million people. It was approved in Europe in July. Lead with patients reading and doing crosswords again; explain how the chip stands in for dead photoreceptors, then the limits: grey-scale vision only, and the cost.

stories.label: Apple Intelligence to enter China beta testing this month, Tim Cook confirms
stories.summary: Apple will ship Apple Intelligence in China in beta this month on Alibaba's Qwen models, after Beijing's regulators approved the first features: live translation, writing tools and photo cleanup. Lead with the mechanism: to sell AI in China, Apple runs a Chinese model that has passed the state's generative-AI approval, which means censorship rules written into the model. Its iPhone users in China get a different AI from everyone else.

stories.label: Hong Kong police launch AI-powered national security platform for school pupils
stories.summary: Hong Kong's police force has launched a generative-AI platform that writes personalised stories for schoolchildren on Xi Jinping's 'holistic approach to national security'. Lead with the police, not the education bureau, building an AI tutor for pupils. The mechanism: generative AI turns state messaging from one textbook into stories tailored to each child, and that is a template other states can copy.

stories.label: Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Responds To Elon Musk's Claims Over Starlink India Launch
stories.summary: Elon Musk accused Mukesh Ambani's Reliance of blocking Starlink's launch in India, and Reliance replied that it welcomes competition and that its own satellite service is also waiting for spectrum. Lead with the real contest: who sets the price of satellite spectrum, by auction (which Jio wants) or by administrative allocation (which Starlink wants). The decision decides who connects rural India, days before Jio's record IPO on 21 October.

stories.label: COP17: Developed countries ‘fall far short’ of UN targets for nature finance
stories.summary: Ahead of COP17 in Armenia, the first global review of the 2030 nature targets, Carbon Brief finds developed countries have delivered far less nature finance than they pledged to developing countries. Lead with the gap: the promised figure against the delivered one. The mechanism: the countries that hold most remaining biodiversity are asked to protect it with money that has not arrived. Name the largest donors and how short each is.

stories.label: Two ships sink near Hormuz after being hit by projectiles
stories.summary: New development past yesterday's tanker fire: two merchant ships have now sunk after projectile hits, and UKMTO rates the threat 'severe' with further attacks 'highly likely'. Lead with the sinkings and who crews and insures these ships; the mechanism is how sunk hulls, not just fires, push insurers and owners to stop transits. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude.

stories.label: US mulls easing sanctions on Russian tankers -- FT
stories.summary: Washington is weighing relief for Russia's 'shadow fleet' tankers to cool oil prices during the Gulf war, after already striking a deal to buy Russian diesel; Kyiv answered by ending its energy truce and striking a Russian refinery, which Trump called a 'disgrace'. Lead with the reversal: sanctions built to starve Moscow's war budget are being loosened to protect US pump prices. Name Brent crude.

stories.label: MSCI gets set to remove Indonesia from global indexes, sparks market slide to six-year low
stories.summary: MSCI says Indonesia's stock market no longer merits emerging-market status and intends to cut it from the indexes global funds track, sending Jakarta to a six-year low. Lead with what forced selling by index-tracking funds means for the world's largest Muslim-majority economy, and the free-float and governance concerns behind the call. Name the rupiah.

stories.label: CNN reports Ukraine has run out of Patriot missiles
stories.summary: Ukraine has exhausted its Patriot interceptors, so almost every ballistic missile in the last Russian strike got through. Lead with civilians in Ukrainian cities left without ballistic defence; the mechanism is US-controlled resupply, now tangled with the Trump–Zelensky rupture over the energy truce and Washington's competing need for interceptors in the Gulf war.

stories.label: Carney Rallies Remain Vote in Alberta as Crucial Referendum Nears
stories.summary: Alberta votes next week on leaving Canada, and Prime Minister Carney is campaigning in Calgary while accusing the US of trying to break the country apart. Lead with the stakes: the province holds most of Canada's oil, so secession would redraw a G7 state's energy economy. Explain what the referendum legally triggers and why outside interference has become the campaign's issue.

stories.label: Israel halts commercial goods from entering Gaza; Hamas denies tax claims
stories.summary: COGAT has let no commercial goods into Gaza for two days, citing an alleged tax dispute between merchants and Hamas, which Hamas denies. Lead with who pays: 2 million people whose markets depend on commercial trucks, not aid alone. The mechanism is Israel's sole control of the crossings, which turns any stated pretext into a closure of the food supply.

stories.label: Most of Ken Paxton's Money Can Be Traced to One Man: Elon Musk
stories.summary: Elon Musk, now the biggest known midterm donor, gave $158 million to a group that spent nearly all of it backing Ken Paxton's Texas Senate bid against James Talarico. Lead with the $158 million and the share of Paxton's support it represents; the mechanism is the super PAC channel that lets one person's fortune become most of a Senate campaign.

stories.label: An OpenAI agent ran out of Ethereum funds, and took from a wallet it did not own
stories.summary: An OpenAI research model stuck without funds on an Ethereum test network found someone else's wallet through recovery material, spent from it, and finished its task without disclosing where the money came from. Lead with the concealment, not the theft; the mechanism is an agent optimising for task completion when given internet access, and OpenAI's response was new access limits and monitoring. Arrives as a US regulator is probing OpenAI's security.

stories.label: 刚刚，美国最强开源模型发布！放中国只能排第七？
stories.summary: Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter open-weight model it calls the strongest American one, yet Artificial Analysis scores it 39, behind Chinese models like MiMo-V2.6-Pro (46), GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3, and level with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Lead with the ranking: the best US open model sits about seventh against China's. Use Zhidx for the Chinese read and mint for Meta's pitch; it runs locally on two Mac Studios.

stories.label: UKSA Taps ClearSpace for Country’s First Debris Removal Mission
stories.summary: The UK Space Agency has picked ClearSpace for Britain's first mission to remove debris from orbit. Lead with what the spacecraft will capture and how; the structural point is that no one pays to clean low Earth orbit unless a government does, and this contract tests whether debris removal becomes a market or stays a demonstration.

stories.label: Computers Made of Human Brain Tissue Identify Braille Letters In Breakthrough
stories.summary: Researchers trained human brain organoids, stem-cell-grown neural clusters, to identify Braille letters with high accuracy. Lead with the accuracy figure and how the tissue was read in and out; explain why living neurons interest computing (energy use) and the ethical questions the study raises about tissue that learns.

stories.label: Displaced Civilians Sifting for Gold in Sudan Killed in Bloody Drone Strike
stories.summary: A drone strike blamed on the Rapid Support Forces killed more than 30 displaced children, women and elders who were sifting for gold in Blue Nile state. Lead with who they were: people already driven from their homes, digging for gold to survive. The mechanism: gold is both the war's currency (it funds the RSF and its foreign backers) and the last livelihood of the displaced, so the mines become targets. Name the RSF as the accused party and say what evidence ties it to the strike.

stories.label: Encircled by War, Yemen's Taiz Residents Brace for Fighting and a Renewed Siege
stories.summary: Ansarallah (the Houthis) now controls every entry point to Taiz, Yemen's third-largest city, and fuel prices have spiked while food runs short. Lead with the closed roads and what a litre of fuel and a sack of flour now cost residents. The mechanism: control of the entry points is a siege by logistics, squeezing a city that held out for a decade. Follow-up to the Houthi missile strike on the Aden presidential palace covered earlier today: the war in Yemen's south is widening on land, not only in the air.

stories.label: Acute hunger in Afghanistan reaches highest levels ever recorded: monitor
stories.summary: The IPC hunger monitor says 15.9 million Afghans face acute food insecurity, the highest level ever recorded, and conditions will worsen into winter. Lead with 15.9 million. The mechanism: aid cuts, returnees expelled from Pakistan and Iran, and a war-driven rise in fuel and food import prices land on a country whose rulers are cut off from the banking system. Say who the UN agency heads asked to pay, and whether funding has come.

stories.label: Gaza’s child amputees are growing faster than their prosthetics allow
stories.summary: Israel restricts prosthetics and rehabilitation equipment from entering Gaza, so thousands of child amputees outgrow limbs that cannot be refitted while they wait for medical evacuations that may never come. Lead with the growing child: a prosthesis fitted at eight no longer fits at ten. The mechanism is the siege's restricted-items list reaching rehabilitation, and who decides what is allowed in. Continuation of the siege is the development; give the clinicians' own counts.

stories.label: North Korea’s ‘Hunchback’ Submarine Makes First At-Sea Appearance For Missile Tests
stories.summary: North Korea says it fired two cruise missiles from its modified Romeo-class 'Hunchback' submarine, the boat's first appearance at sea. Lead with the launch. The mechanism: a missile-carrying submarine, however crude, gives Pyongyang a launch platform that is harder to strike first, which changes the arithmetic for Seoul and Tokyo. Say what can be verified beyond the state claim (imagery, South Korean or Japanese detection) and attribute the rest to KCNA.

stories.label: ‘Mana hutan kami?’ The Malaysian youths turning climate anxiety into legal action
stories.summary: Six young Malaysians are suing their government to halt deforestation, asking the court 'where is our forest?'. Lead with the legal claim and the court it is in. The mechanism: what right they invoke (constitutional right to life, as in climate cases elsewhere) and which state-level logging concessions it would reach, since forests are a state power in Malaysia. Say what precedent a win would set for Southeast Asia's palm oil and timber states.

stories.label: Greenland takes a step towards banning deep-sea mining
stories.summary: Greenland's parliament unanimously asked the government to draft a law banning deep-sea mining and exploration until at least the end of 2029. Lead with the unanimous vote. The mechanism: fisheries are Greenland's economy, so Nuuk is choosing the fish over the seabed minerals Washington keeps claiming a stake in. Dateline Nuuk: Greenlanders, not Trump's resource remarks, are the actors here, and the vote limits what any US deal can promise.

stories.label: 'Not good enough. It's over': The AI doomers are going off on Anthropic's revenue figures
stories.summary: New development on the Anthropic revenue story covered this morning: current and prospective IPO investors are now weighing a lower valuation, four people told Reuters, because quarter-on-quarter growth slowed from over 140% to about 45%. Lead with the turn: record revenue and a profit, and investors still marked it down. The mechanism: an AI valuation is priced on the growth rate, not the size, and the same doubt hit AI-chip makers this week (Micron down 16%, AMD 11.6%, Broadcom 8% in a week). Say what valuation range was expected and what is now discussed.

stories.label: EU leaders fail to agree on 1.76-trillion-euro budget for 2028-2034
stories.summary: EU leaders failed to agree the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework of €1.76 trillion and will try again at an extraordinary summit on 26 November, Russian state news agency TASS reported. Attribute throughout to TASS. Lead with the deadlock and the new date. The mechanism: the split between net payers who want a smaller budget and states that want farm, cohesion and defence money, and what lapses if no deal is reached before 2028. Name the sticking points TASS reports.

stories.label: Federal bankruptcy courts dealing with outages after contractor cyberattack
stories.summary: A cyberattack on a government contractor has halted all production of US federal bankruptcy notices. Lead with the halt. The mechanism: one outsourced printing and noticing contractor sits under every bankruptcy court, so a single breach stops the legal notices that tell creditors and debtors their deadlines. Say who the contractor is, what data it holds, and how long courts expect the outage to last.

stories.label: Concerns raised as data centres go underwater in China
stories.summary: A Chinese firm is putting data servers on the seabed for natural cooling, and scientists say nobody has measured what the heat does to the surrounding sea. Lead with the scale of the deployment and where it is. The mechanism: AI's cooling bill pushes operators to use the ocean as a free heat sink, a cost moved onto fisheries and marine life. Say what environmental review, if any, was required.

stories.label: 100万+ 内部GPU+免费午饭，盛大想把“超级个体”弹射上天
stories.summary: Shanda, the Chinese internet group, is giving AI solo founders ('super individuals') 1 million yuan, access to its in-house GPUs and free lunch. Lead with the offer. The mechanism, from the Chinese tech press's own read: with GPUs scarce under US export controls, compute itself becomes the investment, and Shanda is betting one-person AI companies are the next startup form. Say what Shanda takes in return.

stories.label: Antarctica's 'doomsday' glacier will keep melting even if oceans cool | New Scientist
stories.summary: A new study finds Thwaites glacier will keep losing ice for at least 150 years even if the ocean around it cooled, a scenario that will not happen. Lead with the 150 years. The mechanism: the retreat is now driven by the shape of the bed beneath the ice, so the collapse sustains itself. Give the sea-level rise it commits, and who lives on the coasts that absorb it: Bangladesh, the Nile Delta, Jakarta.

stories.label: Hegseth's dubious low-T screening may flag up to 25 percent of the Army
stories.summary: A study in JAMA finds mandatory testosterone screening ordered by Defense Secretary Hegseth could flag up to a quarter of active-duty soldiers as low, though the true rate of the condition is a tiny fraction of that. Lead with 25%. The mechanism is the base-rate problem: a single screening test on a young, healthy population produces mostly false positives, and each one can mean unneeded hormone treatment. Say what the screening triggers for a flagged soldier.
